chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdillah ibn Jabalah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir and Abdillah, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) granted the covenant of protection (al-dhimmah) to some people from the people of Najran in exchange for seventy cloaks, and did not grant it to anyone else besides them.

key_terms.أَهْلِ نَجْرَانَ: People of Najran (a prominent Christian tribe/community in Arabia)
key_terms.الذِّمَّةَ: Covenant of protection (dhimmah), a treaty granting security and rights to non-Muslims under Islamic rule
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ بُرْدًا: Seventy cloaks (burd), a type of garment used here as a specific form of payment or tribute

ai.seo_question: What was the specific exchange for the covenant of protection granted to the people of Najran by the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records a specific instance where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) granted the covenant of protection (*dhimmah*) to the Christians of Najran in exchange for seventy cloaks (*burd*), a unique arrangement not applied to others. This narration highlights the flexibility of early Islamic treaties and the Prophet's authority to establish distinct financial or material terms for specific communities, a precedent often discussed in Shia jurisprudence regarding *khumus* and treaty obligations.
